title: Infectious and non-infectious diseases

2026-11-12T17:07:13Z recheck: the fresh check agreed with the fix, cleared with the fix

match.reason: The closest bank point only covers types of non-infectious disease at Year 12 depth, while the new point is a Years 9 and 10 contrast between infectious and non-infectious diseases, so it is a different and broader idea at a different depth.

draft.title: Infectious and non-infectious diseases
card: a disease caused by a pathogen, a tiny organism that causes disease. It can spread from one person to another. Influenza is an example.
a disease that is not caused by a pathogen and cannot spread between people. Type 2 diabetes is an example.
Non-infectious diseases can come from genes, lifestyle or the environment. Lifestyle means habits such as diet and exercise. Environment includes things like air pollution or sun exposure.
A cause can be a mix. Skin cancer can come from sun exposure, which is the environment, and also from a person's genes. It still cannot be caught from another person.
draft.remember: Infectious diseases come from pathogens and can spread between people. Non-infectious diseases do not.

a.q: Which statement best explains why type 2 diabetes is a non-infectious disease?
opts: It is not caused by a pathogen, so it cannot spread
It only affects older people, so it cannot spread
It is not serious, so it cannot spread
It lasts a long time, so it cannot spread
a.why: A non-infectious disease is not caused by a pathogen, so it cannot pass from one person to another. How long a disease lasts, or whom it affects, does not decide whether it is infectious.
a.clue: Think about what causes an infectious disease.

b.q: Priya has a skin cancer caused by many years of strong sun exposure. Her classmates worry they could catch it from her. What is the best reply?
opts: It is non-infectious, so it cannot spread between people
It is infectious, because the sun acts as a pathogen
It is infectious, but only through close touch
It is non-infectious, because only genes cause such diseases
b.why: Sun exposure is part of the environment, and no pathogen is involved, so the disease cannot spread between people. The last option is tempting but wrong: non-infectious diseases can come from genes, lifestyle or the environment, not only genes.
b.clue: Is a pathogen involved, or is the cause something else?

a.best: It is not caused by a pathogen, so it cannot spread

b.best: It is non-infectious, so it cannot spread between people

problems.detail: The card defines a pathogen as 'a tiny organism that causes disease', then gives influenza as its example. Influenza is caused by a virus, and viruses are not usually classed as organisms. Some pathogens, such as tapeworms, are also not tiny. A safer wording would be 'a microorganism or other agent, such as a virus, that causes disease'.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer, and the explanations agree with the card. The card's definition of a pathogen as 'a tiny organism' is inaccurate, because its own example, influenza, is caused by a virus, which is not usually called an organism.
